text:
The most powerful refutation is that Bentham’s felicific calculus falsely assumes all pleasures and pains are commensurable on a single quantitative scale, when in fact they differ irreducibly in kind and quality. This objection, associated with Mill, shows the calculus cannot meaningfully measure or compare what actually makes lives go well or badly. It is therefore not merely impractical but conceptually incoherent as a measure of well-being.

CONFIDENCE: 92
